NON-COMPETITION AND NON-SOLICITATION AGREEMENT

This Non-Competition and Non-Solicitation Agreement (this "Agreement") is made as of April 14, 2026 by PRIYA VENKATARAMAN (the "Seller") in favor of CORVID BIOWORKS, INC., a Delaware corporation (the "Buyer").

RECITALS

Under a Stock Purchase Agreement of even date (the "Purchase Agreement"), the Buyer is acquiring all of the outstanding equity of Larkspur Assay Systems, Inc. (the "Company") from the Seller for $34,000,000 in cash, of which $6,800,000 is allocated to the goodwill of the Company's business. The Seller founded the Company, has served as its Chief Executive Officer for eleven years, and holds its customer relationships, pricing history, and assay know-how. The Buyer would not acquire the Company without this Agreement, and the Seller acknowledges that this Agreement is a material inducement to the Buyer and that the consideration under the Purchase Agreement is paid in part for it.

1. NON-COMPETITION. For five (5) years after the Closing, the Seller will not, directly or indirectly, own, manage, operate, control, or be employed by or consult for any business that develops, manufactures, or sells clinical diagnostic assays for oncology indications anywhere in the United States, Canada, or the European Union, which is the territory in which the Company conducted that business as of the Closing. The Seller may own up to 2% of a publicly traded company as a passive investor.

2. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. For five (5) years after the Closing, the Seller will not solicit for employment, or hire, any person employed by the Company or the Buyer at the Closing or during the twelve months before it, except through a general advertisement not targeted at them.

3. NON-SOLICITATION OF CUSTOMERS. For five (5) years after the Closing, the Seller will not solicit, or accept business from, any customer of the Company as of the Closing or during the twenty-four months before it, in respect of any product competitive with the Company's.

4. CONFIDENTIALITY. The Seller will not use or disclose the Company's confidential information at any time. Nothing in this Agreement prohibits the Seller from reporting a possible violation of law to a government agency, or from making a disclosure protected by 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b).

5. SALE-OF-BUSINESS COVENANT. The parties intend this Agreement to be a covenant given in connection with the sale of the goodwill of a business, enforceable under California Business and Professions Code § 16601 and the corresponding statutes of every other jurisdiction in which it is enforced, and not a covenant ancillary to employment. The Seller is selling all of the Seller's equity in the Company, and the consideration allocated to goodwill is stated above.

6. REASONABLENESS. The Seller acknowledges that the duration, territory, and scope of these covenants are reasonable and no greater than necessary to protect the goodwill the Buyer is purchasing, and that the Seller has the means to earn a living outside the restricted business.

7. BLUE-PENCIL. If a court finds any covenant unenforceable as written, it shall be reformed to the maximum extent enforceable rather than struck.

8. REMEDIES. A breach would cause irreparable harm for which damages are an inadequate remedy, and the Buyer is entitled to injunctive relief without posting bond, in addition to damages. The restricted period is tolled during any period of breach.

9. INDEPENDENT COUNSEL. The Seller has been represented by independent counsel of the Seller's own choosing in negotiating this Agreement and the Purchase Agreement.

10. GOVERNING LAW. Delaware law governs. Venue lies in the Delaware Court of Chancery.

/s/ Priya Venkataraman
PRIYA VENKATARAMAN, Seller

CORVID BIOWORKS, INC.
